lead_headline: Council Declines to Override City Manager on Frontline Farming Lease

type_specific.meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council held its June 16, 2026 business meeting, featuring extensive public comment on three major community topics: the proposed Frontline Farming lease termination at Majestic View Nature Center, the pending Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (KSAP), and the Avalon/Wellby Gardens conditional use permit reconsideration request. The council approved three resolutions — a waste hauling fee increase, a CDBG annual action plan submission, and an Arvada Center funding release (with one recusal) — and passed two consent agenda items. Council members declined to intervene in the Frontline Farming lease decision, citing the city manager's operational authority under city code.

presentations.topic: City Manager Statement — Frontline Farming Lease Termination
presentations.presenter_role: Vibrant Community Neighborhoods Director, City of Arvada
prose_paragraphs: Following approximately three hours of public comment, VCN Director Ryan Stevenson provided the city's formal statement on the Frontline Farming lease termination. Stevenson acknowledged Frontline's community contributions but stated the decision followed documented lease compliance, operational, and safety concerns addressed through meetings, site visits, and a formal notice issued in May 2025. He described the critical factor as the discovery in March of an unauthorized electrical installation connected to city-owned infrastructure, which a staff member nearly struck with a pickaxe; staff determined the live wire was unencased, not permitted, not approved by the city, and not compliant with electrical code. The city is allowing Frontline to continue operating through the growing season ending in November 2026 to allow for transition.

presenter_quotes.speaker: Ryan Stevenson
presenter_quotes.text: A significant factor in the city's decision came this past March with this discovery of an unauthorized electrical installation connected to city-owned infrastructure that crossed portions of the outdoor classroom and nature play area.
presenter_quotes.context_excerpt: City staff continued working with frontline leadership throughout the following year in an effort to address concerns and maintain a productive working relationship. A significant factor in the city's decision came this past March with this discovery of an unauthorized electrical installation connected to city-owned infrastructure that crossed portions of the outdoor classroom and nature play area.

presenter_quotes.speaker: Ryan Stevenson
presenter_quotes.text: This unauthorized installation was a serious safety hazard because it was a live electrical wire that was unencased and at points partially buried. It was only discovered when a staff member nearly struck it with a pickaxe. Had the wire been struck, it could have been fatal.
presenter_quotes.context_excerpt: After investigating the inst uh the installation, city staff determined it had not been approved by the city, had not been permitted, and did not comply with uh with applicable electrical code requirements. consent_agenda.official_title: R26-042, a resolution accepting an annexation petition for annexing certain land into the city of Arvvada, Revival Industrial, a 5.3980 acre parcel of land approximately located south of State Highway 72 east of 15350 State Highway 72 in the city of Arvvada, county of Jefferson, state of Colorado, finding said petition substantially compliant with CRS31-12-1071 and setting a public hearing for July 21st 2026 at 6:15 p.m. for city council to determine whether the area meets requirements of CRS 31-12-104 and 105 and is considered eligible for annexation
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Accepts a petition to annex a 5.4-acre parcel near State Highway 72 into Arvada and schedules a public hearing for July 21, 2026, to formally determine whether the land is eligible for annexation.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-043 a resolution authorizing an agreement by and between the city of Arvvada and Adonia Transportation Solutions LLC for traffic signal and intersection improvements at West 64th Avenue and Easley Road at West 63rd Avenue and McIntyre Parkway project number 24-TC-01 in an amount not to exceed 1,231,762
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Authorizes a contract with Adonia Transportation Solutions LLC (up to $1,231,762) to install traffic signals and make intersection improvements at West 64th/Easley Road and West 63rd/McIntyre Parkway.

resolutions.official_title: R26-044, a resolution adopting the amended fee schedule for the waste hauling program pursuant to chapter 90 solid waste of the Arvvada city code and authorizing the fourth amendment to an agreement between the city of Arvvada and Allied Waste Transportation doing business as Republic Services of Denver for residential solid waste collection services thereby increasing waste service fees
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Updates the city's solid waste and recycling fee schedule effective July 1, 2026, passing through a Republic Services price increase (up to 3.5% per their contract) plus a 5-cent city program fee increase; monthly customer bills will rise by approximately 48 cents to 80 cents depending on cart size.

resolutions.official_title: R26-045, a resolution authorizing submission of the 2026 annual action plan for the 2026 Community Development Block Grant, CDBG, funding
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Authorizes submission of Arvada's 2026 CDBG annual action plan to HUD, allocating $460,479 in federal grant funds toward public services ($69,171), program administration ($92,095), and the Gold Strike Park project ($299,313).

resolutions.official_title: R26-046, a resolution authorizing the release of the second half of previously approved advanced funds to the Arvvada Center in the amount of $812,000
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Releases the second half ($812,000) of previously approved advance funds to the Arvada Center. Councilmember Lovisone recused herself due to her part-time employment with the Arvada Center.
